subject: Request for security testing artifacts — exec summary access & redaction terms
messages:
From: Alex Garner <alex.garner@sentinelfin.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dana Morris <dana.morris@glenwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: security testing artifacts for procurement review

Hi Rishi,

We're progressing toward a security review for the Glenwood Financial procurement committee. As part of the packet they'd like to review both an executive summary of your most recent independent security assessment and the full test report (redacted where appropriate).

Two quick questions:
- What level of redaction do you require for the full report (hostnames, PoC code, remediation timelines)?
- Do you require a mutual NDA or will a redacted executive summary suffice for initial assessment?

If helpful, I can route an NDA template from our legal team. We are on a tight schedule — procurement would like the materials by Oct 8 if possible.

Thanks,
Alex Garner
Security Lead, Sentinel Financial (Glenwood Review)
alex.garner@sentinelfin.com
+1 (415) 555-0198
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Garner <alex.garner@sentinelfin.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: security testing artifacts for procurement review

Alex — thanks for the note and the timeline. We can share an executive summary quickly; the full assessment requires signing a mutual NDA and a brief redaction pass. High-level answers:

- Typical redactions: internal hostnames, exact PoC exploit code/snippets, on-prem customer IP, and raw log extracts that contain customer data. We do not redact remediation status or timelines.
- For procurement-only review, a redacted executive summary often suffices. For your security team/auditor access to the full report, we need a mutual NDA that includes an auditor-access clause and a restriction on public distribution.

I attached a short redaction checklist (Redaction_Checklist_v1.pdf) to show what we redact and why. Laura (cc'd) can provide a remediation update and an internal tracker. If you send your NDA template we can route to legal; otherwise we can provide our mutual NDA draft.

I expect we can get the exec summary over by Oct 5 and the redacted full report once the NDA is executed.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive — Enterprise | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Garner <alex.garner@sentinelfin.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: security testing artifacts for procurement review

Alex — quick technical note from the security team:

Summary of approach for the report share and remediation:
- What we can share immediately: an executive summary that includes scope, methodology, severity breakdown, and remediation status (summary level).
- What we will remove from the full report: environment hostnames/IPs, exploit PoC code or step-by-step reproduction instructions that would materially enable exploitation, raw memory dumps, and customer-identifying screenshots.
- What remains visible: vulnerability descriptions, CVSS-equivalent severity, evidence summary (high-level), and remediation notes with dates.

Current remediation status (as of 2026-10-04):
- Findings total: 12 (5 Critical, 4 High, 3 Medium)
- Resolved: 6 (2 Critical, 3 High, 1 Medium) — fixes verified via retest
- In progress / planned: 6 (remediation timelines included per finding in the tracker)

I've attached our remediation tracker (Remediation_Tracker_20261004.xlsx). If you need an auditor to validate fixes we can discuss controlled access under the NDA (read-only view, monitored session).

Laura Bennett
Head of Security Operations | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
From: Alex Garner <alex.garner@sentinelfin.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dana Morris <dana.morris@glenwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: security testing artifacts for procurement review

Thanks Rishi/Laura — that level of detail sounds good. Two items from legal/procurement:
1) Our legal team prefers to send our mutual NDA template (they ask that the vendor mark any items the vendor needs redacted). I'll attach it by end of day.
2) Procurement needs the executive summary unredacted for all content except PoC code and direct exploit instructions; they want remediation timelines visible.

We can sign your mutual NDA if you attach it. Also, will you accept our auditors (third-party) to view the redacted full report under the same NDA?

Alex
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Garner <alex.garner@sentinelfin.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: security testing artifacts for procurement review

Alex — we uploaded a short mutual NDA draft (Mutual_NDA_SentinelFin_RevA.docx) to speed legal review and included an auditor-access clause with the following constraints:
- Auditor access allowed if auditor signs the same NDA and access is scoped to read-only viewing under monitored session.
- We exclude reproduction of PoC code and attestations that would disclose exploit details.
- We add a narrow carve-out allowing disclosure to subcontracted auditors but require prior notice and limited retention.

If that aligns your legal team's needs, please countersign or send redlines. Once NDA is executed we'll send the redacted executive summary immediately and schedule a window for an auditor read-only review of the full report.

DocuSign: https://na1.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abc-nda-2026

Thanks,
Rishi
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Garner <alex.garner@sentinelfin.com>, Dana Morris <dana.morris@glenwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec summary and NDA — delivery

Alex/Dana — thanks for working through this. We received the countersigned NDA via DocuSign this morning (link above). Per the agreement, please find the redacted executive summary attached (Exec_Summary_Redacted_20261007.pdf).

Highlights in the exec summary:
- Assessment scope: public-facing inference endpoints, auth layers, and internal model caching services.
- Severity snapshot: 12 findings (5 Critical, 4 High, 3 Medium).
- Resolved vs outstanding: 6 resolved, 6 with planned timelines (dates included).
- Redaction note: exploit PoC and environment hostnames removed; remediation notes preserved.

Next steps we propose:
1) If your procurement team accepts the exec summary, we'll provision a monitored, read-only session for your auditor to view the redacted full report (date options: Oct 11–13).
2) If further detail is needed on a specific finding, we can schedule a short 30-minute call with Laura and an on-call engineer.

Attachments: Exec_Summary_Redacted_20261007.pdf (PDF, 45 KB)

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive — Enterprise | Redwood Inference
